candidate.blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — perform skin assessment and implement measures to maintain skin/tissue integrity
candidate.educational_objective: Identify a Stage 2 pressure injury from partial-thickness skin loss with exposed dermis and no obscuring tissue.

options.A: Stage 1 pressure injury because the wound remains superficial and no subcutaneous tissue or deeper structures are visible.
options.B: Deep tissue pressure injury because exposed red-pink tissue indicates damage beneath intact or partially disrupted skin.
options.C: Unstageable pressure injury because the nurse cannot determine depth until all devitalized tissue has been removed from the wound.
options.D: Stage 2 pressure injury because the finding represents partial-thickness skin loss with exposed dermis and no obscuring tissue.

candidate.rationale: The described wound is consistent with a Stage 2 pressure injury: partial-thickness skin loss with exposed dermis and no visible adipose, granulation tissue, slough, or eschar. Stage 1 requires intact skin; unstageable injury requires obscuring tissue that prevents determination of depth.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Stage 2 pressure injury is partial-thickness skin loss with exposed dermis and lacks visible adipose, granulation tissue, slough or eschar.

candidate.stem: A pressure injury over the sacrum has partial-thickness skin loss with exposed, moist red-pink dermis. Adipose tissue, granulation tissue, slough, and eschar are not visible. How should the nurse stage this injury?
